chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him, 'A man acknowledges a debt to an heir?' He said, 'That is permissible if he is wealthy (liable to pay).'

key_terms.إِقْرَار: Acknowledgment or confession of a debt or right
key_terms.مَلِيّاً: Wealthy or having sufficient assets to pay the debt

ai.seo_question: Is a dying man's acknowledgment of debt to an heir valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a dying man’s acknowledgment of a debt to an heir is valid if he was wealthy (*maliyyan*), thereby preventing the presumption of fraud in estate distribution. This ruling addresses the Shia legal concern of *ikrar* (acknowledgment) in *al-marad* (the illness of death), ensuring that debts are not fabricated to reduce the shares of other heirs. The condition of wealth serves as a safeguard, implying that a poor person’s large debt acknowledgment might be suspect due to lack of means to repay.
